1→# Crowd Simulation
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Houdini's crowd system simulates large numbers of animated characters (agents) using a lightweight packed agent representation. Agents carry embedded animation clips, collision shapes, and layers, and are driven through a state machine in DOPs. The system is built on the Agent primitive type -- a packed prim with skeletal animation, shape libraries, and clip blending.
     6→
     7→## SOP-Level Setup Chain
     8→
     9→```
    10→character_fbx -> agent -> agentlayer (optional) -> agentclip (additional clips)
    11→    -> crowdsource -> crowdstate (initial state assignment)
    12→    -> dopnet(crowdsolver) -> dopimport -> filecache
    13→```
    14→
    15→For import to LOPs: `filecache` -> `sopimport` LOP
    16→
    17→## Agent Setup
    18→
    19→### agent SOP
    20→
    21→Creates an Agent primitive from an FBX/BVH/character file. This is the entry point for all crowd work.
    22→
    23→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
    24→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
    25→| Agent Name | `agentname` | agent1 | Unique name for this agent type |
    26→| Input | `input` | FBX File | Source type: FBX, BVH, or Character Rig |
    27→| FBX File | `fbxfile` | (empty) | Path to .fbx character file |
    28→| Convert Units | `convertunits` | 1 | Auto-convert units (cm to m) |
    29→| Clip Name | `clipname` | (auto) | Name for the default animation clip |
    30→| Locomotion Joint | `locomotionjoint` | (auto) | Root joint for locomotion (usually Hips) |
    31→| Locomotion | `locomotion` | 1 | Enable in-place clip conversion |
    32→
    33→**Locomotion**: When enabled, the agent SOP strips the root joint's forward translation from the clip and stores it as `locomotion speed`. The crowd solver then moves the agent point in world space at that speed. This is essential -- without it, agents will slide or moonwalk.
    34→
    35→### agentclip SOP
    36→
    37→Adds additional animation clips to an existing agent.
    38→
    39→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
    40→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
    41→| Clip Name | `name` | clip1 | Name for this clip |
    42→| Source | `source` | FBX Animation File | Where to get the clip |
    43→| FBX File | `fbxfile` | (empty) | Path to FBX with animation |
    44→| Start/End Frame | `startend` | 1/240 | Clip frame range |
    45→| Locomotion | `locomotion` | 1 | Convert to in-place clip |
    46→| Locomotion Joint | `locomotionjoint` | (same as agent) | Root joint name |
    47→
    48→### agentlayer SOP
    49→
    50→Defines geometry layers on an agent -- different shapes that can be swapped for variation.
    51→
    52→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
    53→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
    54→| Layer Name | `layername` | default | Name of this layer |
    55→| Source | `source` | Current Layer | Inherit existing or start fresh |
    56→| Shape Transform | `shapetransform#` | (varies) | Which joint a shape is bound to |
    57→| Shape Geometry | `shapegeo#` | (varies) | Geometry for this shape |
    58→| Deforming | `deforming#` | 1 | Whether shape deforms with skeleton |
    59→
    60→Layers allow swapping armor pieces, helmets, weapons, or clothing per agent. Each layer is a named set of shape bindings.
    61→
    62→### agentprep SOP
    63→
    64→Prepares agents for simulation. Configures collision shapes, foot joints, and terrain adaptation.
    65→
    66→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
    67→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
    68→| Agent Name | `agentname` | (auto) | Which agent type to configure |
    69→| Show Guide | `showguide` | 1 | Display collision/foot guides |
    70→| Enable Terrain Adapt | `enableterrain` | 0 | Set up terrain following |
    71→| Hip Joint | `hipjoint` | Hips | Joint for terrain offset |
    72→| Foot Joints | `leftfoot`/`rightfoot` | (auto) | Foot joints for foot locking |
    73→| Lower Limb Joints | `leftlowerleg`/`rightlowerleg` | (auto) | Knee joints for IK |
    74→| Upper Limb Joints | `leftupperleg`/`rightupperleg` | (auto) | Hip joints for IK |
    75→| Ankle Offset | `ankleoffset` | 0.0 | Vertical offset from ankle to sole |
    76→
    77→**Critical**: Agent Prep must be connected before the DOP network. Without it, terrain adaptation and foot locking will not work. The foot/leg joint names must match the skeleton exactly.
    78→
    79→## Crowd Source
    80→
    81→### crowdsource SOP
    82→
    83→Places agents in the scene with initial positions, orientations, and state assignments.
    84→
    85→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
    86→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
    87→| Number of Agents | `numagents` | 10 | How many agents to scatter |
    88→| Randomize | `randomize` | 1 | Randomize positions |
    89→| Area Shape | `areashape` | Circle | Scatter area (Circle, Rectangle, Custom) |
    90→| Area Size | `areasize` | 10 | Scatter radius/size |
    91→| Formation | `formation` | None | Grid, Circle, Custom |
    92→| Agent Group | `agentgroup` | (empty) | Assign to named group |
    93→| Initial State | `initialstate` | (empty) | Starting state machine state |
    94→| Initial Clip | `initialclip` | (auto) | Starting animation clip |
    95→| Randomize Clip Offset | `randomclipoffset` | 1 | Offset clip start time per agent |
    96→| Max Initial Speed | `maxinitspeed` | 1.0 | Random initial speed range |
    97→
    98→### Formation Types
    99→
   100→| Formation | Parameter Value | Description |
   101→|-----------|----------------|-------------|
   102→| None | `0` | Random scatter in area |
   103→| Grid | `1` | Regular grid, set rows/columns |
   104→| Circle | `2` | Ring formation |
   105→| Custom Geometry | `3` | Points from input geometry define positions |
   106→
   107→For custom formations, wire geometry with points into crowdsource input 2. Each point becomes an agent position. Add `@orient` (quaternion) on input points to control facing direction.
   108→
   109→### crowdstate SOP
   110→
   111→Assigns initial states to agents before simulation.
   112→
   113→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
   114→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
   115→| State Name | `statename` | idle | Name of the state to assign |
   116→| Group | `group` | (empty) | Apply to specific agent group |
   117→| Randomize | `randomize` | 0 | Randomly assign from multiple states |
   118→
   119→## Crowd Simulation (DOPs)
   120→
   121→### DOP Network Setup
   122→
   123→```
   124→crowdsource -> dopnet -> dopimport
   125→```
   126→
   127→Inside the DOP network:
   128→
   129→```
   130→crowdobject -> groundplane (optional) -> crowdsolver -> output
   131→```
   132→
   133→### crowdobject DOP
   134→
   135→Imports the crowd from SOPs into the DOP simulation.
   136→
   137→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
   138→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
   139→| SOP Path | `soppath` | (auto) | Path to SOP crowd source |
   140→| Use Object Transform | `useobjecttransform` | 0 | Apply object-level transform |
   141→
   142→### crowdsolver DOP
   143→
   144→The core simulation engine. Runs the state machine, blends clips, handles avoidance, applies forces.
   145→
   146→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
   147→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
   148→| Substeps | `substeps` | 1 | Solver substeps |
   149→| Avoidance Force | `avoidanceforce` | 1.0 | Strength of inter-agent avoidance |
   150→| Avoidance Radius | `anticipatetime` | 2.0 | Look-ahead time for avoidance (seconds) |
   151→| Max Speed | `maxspeed` | 2.0 | Maximum agent speed (m/s) |
   152→| Max Rotation Speed | `maxrotspeed` | 120 | Max turning rate (deg/s) |
   153→| Max Accel | `maxaccel` | 5.0 | Maximum acceleration |
   154→| Terrain Following | `terrain` | 0 | Enable terrain snap |
   155→| Terrain Object | `terrainobject` | (empty) | DOP object or SOP path for terrain |
   156→| Foot Locking | `enablefootlocking` | 0 | Enable IK foot plant |
   157→
   158→### State Machine
   159→
   160→Crowd behavior is driven by a state machine. Each state plays a clip, applies forces, and checks triggers for transitions.
   161→
   162→#### crowdstate DOP (inside crowdsolver)
   163→
   164→Defines a behavioral state.
   165→
   166→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
   167→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
   168→| State Name | `statename` | state1 | Unique state name |
   169→| Animation Clips | `clipnames` | (empty) | Clip(s) to play in this state |
   170→| Clip Speed Multiplier | `clipspeedmultiplier` | 1.0 | Speed scale on clip playback |
   171→| Blend Time | `blendtime` | 0.3 | Seconds to blend from previous clip |
   172→| Speed Range | `speedrange` | 0/2 | Min/max agent speed in this state |
   173→| Speed Clip Range | `speedcliprange` | (auto) | Map speed to clip blend |
   174→
   175→#### crowdtrigger DOP
   176→
   177→Defines conditions that cause state transitions.
   178→
   179→| Trigger Type | Parameter | Description |
   180→|-------------|-----------|-------------|
   181→| Time in State | `timeinstate` | Fires after N seconds in current state |
   182→| Proximity to Object | `objectdistance` | Fires when near a specific object |
   183→| Proximity to Agent | `agentdistance` | Fires when near another agent |
   184→| Bounding Box | `boundingbox` | Fires when inside a bounding box |
   185→| Particle Speed | `particlespeed` | Fires at a speed threshold |
   186→| Custom VEX | `customvex` | Fires based on VEX expression |
   187→| Crowd Field | `crowdfield` | Fires based on crowd attribute value |
   188→| Object Attribute | `objectattribute` | Fires based on object attribute |
   189→
   190→#### crowdtransition DOP
   191→
   192→Links a trigger to a state change.
   193→
   194→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
   195→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
   196→| Source State | `sourcestate` | (any) | State to transition from |
   197→| Target State | `targetstate` | (required) | State to transition to |
   198→| Trigger | `trigger` | (required) | Which trigger activates this |
   199→| Duration | `duration` | 0.3 | Transition blend time |
   200→| Priority | `priority` | 0 | Higher priority wins if multiple triggers fire |
   201→
   202→### Example State Machine
   203→
   204→A basic walk-to-run-to-idle cycle:
   205→
   206→```
   207→State: idle (clip=idle_anim, speed=0)
   208→  Trigger: proximity_to_goal (distance < 20)
   209→    -> Transition to: walk
   210→
   211→State: walk (clip=walk_cycle, speed=1.0)
   212→  Trigger: proximity_to_goal (distance < 5)
   213→    -> Transition to: idle
   214→  Trigger: speed_threshold (speed > 1.5)
   215→    -> Transition to: run
   216→
   217→State: run (clip=run_cycle, speed=2.5)
   218→  Trigger: speed_threshold (speed < 1.2)
   219→    -> Transition to: walk
   220→```
   221→
   222→## Terrain Following
   223→
   224→### Setup Requirements
   225→
   226→1. Agent Prep: Enable terrain adaptation, set hip/foot/leg joints
   227→2. Crowd Solver: Enable `terrain` parm, set `terrainobject` to terrain SOP or DOP object
   228→3. Optional: Enable `enablefootlocking` on crowd solver for IK foot plant
   229→
   230→### Terrain Adaptation Parameters (Agent Prep)
   231→
   232→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
   233→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
   234→| Hip Joint | `hipjoint` | Hips | Joint to offset vertically |
   235→| Hip Offset | `hipoffset` | 0.0 | Additional vertical hip offset |
   236→| Back Adjust | `backadjust` | lean | How to handle slopes: lean or tilt |
   237→| Lean Angle | `leanangle` | 15 | Max forward/back lean in degrees |
   238→| Left/Right Foot | `leftfoot`/`rightfoot` | (auto) | Foot joints for terrain snap |
   239→| Ankle Offset | `ankleoffset` | 0.0 | Distance from ankle joint to foot sole |
   240→
   241→### Foot Locking
   242→
   243→Foot locking plants feet on the terrain during the grounded phase of a walk/run cycle. It uses IK on the leg chain to adjust foot positions.
   244→
   245→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
   246→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
   247→| Enable | `enablefootlocking` | 0 | Turn on foot planting |
   248→| Lock Blend Time | `lockblendtime` | 0.1 | Blend into locked position (seconds) |
   249→| Unlock Blend Time | `unlockblendtime` | 0.1 | Blend out of locked position |
   250→| Adjust Hips | `adjusthips` | 1 | Lower hips when feet reach down |
   251→
   252→**Foot lock channels**: The agent clip must have foot-lock metadata indicating which frames each foot is planted. Use `agentclip` SOP's "Locomotion" tab to auto-detect or manually set planted frames via `s@agentrig_footchannel` attributes.
   253→
   254→### Obstacle Avoidance
   255→
   256→Built into the crowd solver. Agents steer away from each other and from DOP objects.
   257→
   258→| Parameter | Name | Default | Description |
   259→|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
   260→| Avoidance Force | `avoidanceforce` | 1.0 | Avoidance strength |
   261→| Anticipation Time | `anticipatetime` | 2.0 | Look-ahead time (seconds) |
   262→| Neighbor Distance | `neighbordist` | 5.0 | Radius to check for neighbors |
   263→| Max Neighbors | `maxneighbors` | 6 | Max neighbors to consider |
   264→| FOV | `fov` | 180 | Agent field of view (degrees) |
   265→| Avoidance Weight | `avoidanceweight` | 1.0 | Blend vs other steering forces |
   266→
   267→For static obstacles, add `staticobject` DOPs. For animated obstacles, use `rbdobject` or `staticobject` with deforming enabled.
   268→
   269→## Agent Variations
   270→
   271→### Shape Variation (Agent Layers)
   272→
   273→Each agent type can have multiple layers. At crowdsource time, assign layers randomly:
   274→
   275→```vex
   276→// In a wrangle after crowdsource:
   277→string layers[] = {"default", "armor_heavy", "armor_light", "casual"};
   278→int idx = int(random(@ptnum) * len(layers));
   279→s@agentcurrentlayer = layers[idx];
   280→```
   281→
   282→Or use the crowdsource SOP's `Layer` parameter to specify randomly from available layers.
   283→
   284→### Clip Variation
   285→
   286→Randomize which animation clip plays per state:
   287→
   288→```vex
   289→// In a wrangle on the crowd source:
   290→float r = random(@ptnum + 31);
   291→if (r < 0.33) s@crowdinitialclip = "walk_01";
   292→else if (r < 0.66) s@crowdinitialclip = "walk_02";
   293→else s@crowdinitialclip = "walk_03";
   294→
   295→// Random clip offset so agents don't sync
   296→f@crowdinitialcliptime = random(@ptnum) * 30.0;
   297→```
   298→
   299→### Material/Style Sheet Variation
   300→
   301→Houdini uses CVEX style sheets to vary materials per agent or per shape. Style sheets are applied at render time without duplicating geometry.
   302→
   303→Key concepts:
   304→- **Target**: Which agents/shapes the override applies to (by agent name, group, or attribute)
   305→- **Override**: What material property to change (diffuse color, texture path, roughness)
   306→
   307→Style sheet JSON structure:
   308→```json
   309→{
   310→  "styles": [
   311→    {
   312→      "target": {"group": "crowd_*", "subTarget": {"shape": "body"}},
   313→      "overrides": {
   314→        "material:parameter": {"diffuseColor": {"type": "random", "min": [0.3,0.2,0.1], "max": [0.8,0.6,0.4]}}
   315→      }
   316→    }
   317→  ]
   318→}
   319→```
   320→
   321→In production, style sheets live in a `.json` file referenced by the render settings. They run at render time (Mantra, Karma CPU) and apply material overrides without modifying agent geometry.
   322→
   323→**Karma XPU note**: CVEX style sheets are NOT supported in Karma XPU (as of Houdini 20/21). Use MaterialX with per-agent primvars instead, or render crowds with Karma CPU.
   324→
   325→### Color/Attribute Variation
   326→
   327→```vex
   328→// Vary color per agent at source time
   329→v@Cd = set(random(@ptnum), random(@ptnum+7), random(@ptnum+13));
   330→
   331→// Vary scale slightly
   332→f@pscale = fit01(random(@ptnum+99), 0.85, 1.15);
   333→
   334→// Store custom attributes for style sheets
   335→f@armor_wear = random(@ptnum + 42);
   336→```
   337→
   338→## Crowd Rendering in Solaris/Karma
   339→
   340→### SOP Import to LOPs
   341→
   342→```
   343→filecache (cached crowd sim) -> sopimport LOP -> materiallibrary -> assignmaterial -> karmarendersettings
   344→```
   345→
   346→The `sopimport` LOP brings agent primitives onto the USD stage. Houdini converts each agent to a USD `PointInstancer` or skeletal `SkelRoot` depending on the pipeline approach.
   347→
   348→### Point Instancer Approach (Recommended for Large Crowds)
   349→
   350→Agents render as point-instanced geometry. Each unique agent type becomes a prototype; each agent in the crowd references a prototype with per-instance transforms.
   351→
   352→| Aspect | Detail |
   353→|--------|--------|
   354→| Node | `sopimport` with agent geometry |
   355→| USD Type | `PointInstancer` |
   356→| Prototype | One per unique agent mesh |
   357→| Performance | Excellent -- GPU instancing, minimal memory |
   358→| Limitation | No per-agent skeletal deformation at render time |
   359→
   360→Best for: background crowds, distant shots, thousands of agents.
   361→
   362→### Skeletal Agent Approach (Hero Crowds)
   363→
   364→Each agent maintains its own skeleton and deforms at render time. More expensive but supports full animation fidelity.
   365→
   366→| Aspect | Detail |
   367→|--------|--------|
   368→| USD Type | `SkelRoot` + `Skeleton` + `SkelAnimation` |
   369→| Deformation | Full per-agent skin deformation |
   370→| Performance | Expensive -- one draw call per agent |
   371→| Limitation | Scales to hundreds, not thousands |
   372→
   373→Best for: foreground/hero crowd members, close-up shots.
   374→
   375→### LOD Strategy
   376→
   377→Use multiple agent layers with decreasing detail:
   378→
   379→| LOD Level | Use Case | Strategy |
   380→|-----------|----------|----------|
   381→| LOD0 (high) | Foreground, < 20m from camera | Full mesh, full skeleton deform |
   382→| LOD1 (mid) | Mid-ground, 20-50m | Reduced mesh, skeletal deform |
   383→| LOD2 (low) | Background, 50-100m | Simple mesh, point instanced |
   384→| LOD3 (billboard) | Far background, > 100m | Card/billboard, no deformation |
   385→
   386→In SOPs, create agent layers per LOD level using `agentlayer` SOP. Switch layers based on camera distance in a post-sim wrangle:
   387→
   388→```vex
   389→float dist = distance(@P, chv("camera_pos"));
   390→if (dist < 20) s@agentcurrentlayer = "lod0";
   391→else if (dist < 50) s@agentcurrentlayer = "lod1";
   392→else if (dist < 100) s@agentcurrentlayer = "lod2";
   393→else s@agentcurrentlayer = "lod3";
   394→```
   395→
   396→### Karma Render Settings for Crowds
   397→
   398→| Parameter | Recommendation | Why |
   399→|-----------|---------------|-----|
   400→| Ray Bias | 0.01 | Avoid self-intersection on instanced geo |
   401→| Max Ray Depth | 4-6 | Crowds rarely need deep bounces |
   402→| Pixel Samples | 6-9 for mid, 16+ for hero | Balance noise vs render time |
   403→| Denoiser | OIDN or OptiX | Essential for noisy crowd backgrounds |
   404→| Motion Blur | Per-agent velocity from sim | Use `v@v` from crowd sim for correct blur |
   405→
   406→## Key VEX Functions for Crowds
   407→
   408→### Agent Introspection
   409→
   410→```vex
   411→// Get the agent's current clip name(s)
   412→string clips[] = agentclipcatalog(0, @ptnum);
   413→
   414→// Get the current clip time
   415→float t = agentcliptime(0, @ptnum, "walk_cycle");
   416→
   417→// Get the current clip weight (for blending)
   418→float w = agentclipweight(0, @ptnum, "walk_cycle");
   419→
   420→// Get all clip names available on this agent
   421→string all_clips[] = agentclipcatalog(0, @ptnum);
   422→
   423→// Get clip length
   424→float len = agentcliplength(0, @ptnum, "walk_cycle");
   425→
   426→// Get the agent's current layer
   427→string layer = agentcurrentlayer(0, @ptnum);
   428→
   429→// Get all available layers
   430→string layers[] = agentlayers(0, @ptnum);
   431→
   432→// Get the agent's name (type)
   433→string name = agentname(0, @ptnum);
   434→```
   435→
   436→### Agent Transform Access
   437→
   438→```vex
   439→// Get a specific joint's world transform
   440→matrix xform = agentworldtransform(0, @ptnum, "Hips");
   441→
   442→// Get a joint's local transform
   443→matrix local_xform = agentlocaltransform(0, @ptnum, "Spine1");
   444→
   445→// Get the joint index by name
   446→int idx = agentrigfind(0, @ptnum, "LeftFoot");
   447→
   448→// Get all joint names
   449→string joints[] = agentrigchildren(0, @ptnum, "Hips");
   450→
   451→// Get parent joint
   452→string parent = agentrigparent(0, @ptnum, "LeftFoot");
   453→```
   454→
   455→### Agent Modification
   456→
   457→```vex
   458→// Set current clip and time
   459→setagentcliptime(0, @ptnum, "idle", 5.0);
   460→setagentclipweight(0, @ptnum, "idle", 1.0);
   461→
   462→// Change layer
   463→setagentcurrentlayer(0, @ptnum, "armor_heavy");
   464→
   465→// Override a joint transform
   466→matrix m = agentworldtransform(0, @ptnum, "Head");
   467→rotate(m, radians(15), {1,0,0});  // tilt head
   468→setagentworldtransform(0, @ptnum, m, "Head");
   469→```
   470→
   471→### Crowd Steering (in POP Wrangle inside Crowd Solver)
   472→
   473→```vex
   474→// Seek toward a target
   475→vector target = chv("target_pos");
   476→vector desired = normalize(target - @P) * ch("max_speed");
   477→vector steer = desired - @v;
   478→@force += steer * ch("seek_weight");
   479→
   480→// Flee from a point
   481→vector threat = chv("threat_pos");
   482→float dist = distance(@P, threat);
   483→if (dist < ch("flee_radius")) {
   484→    vector flee_dir = normalize(@P - threat);
   485→    @force += flee_dir * ch("flee_force") * (1.0 - dist / ch("flee_radius"));
   486→}
   487→```
   488→
   489→### Crowd Attribute Reference
   490→
   491→Key point attributes on crowd agents:
   492→
   493→| Attribute | Type | Description |
   494→|-----------|------|-------------|
   495→| `@P` | vector | Agent world position |
   496→| `@orient` | quaternion | Agent facing direction |
   497→| `@v` | vector | Agent velocity |
   498→| `@up` | vector | Agent up vector |
   499→| `@pscale` | float | Agent scale |
   500→| `s@agentname` | string | Agent type name |
   501→| `s@crowdstate` | string | Current state machine state |
   502→| `s@crowdinitialstate` | string | Starting state |
   503→| `s@crowdinitialclip` | string | Starting animation clip |
   504→| `f@crowdinitialcliptime` | float | Starting clip time offset |
   505→| `f@crowdspeed` | float | Current locomotion speed |
   506→| `f@crowdturnrate` | float | Current turning rate |
   507→| `s@agentcurrentlayer` | string | Active geometry layer |
   508→| `i@crowdactive` | int | Whether agent is active (1) or frozen (0) |
   509→| `f@crowdanimscale` | float | Clip playback speed multiplier |
   510→| `i@id` | int | Unique agent ID (stable across frames) |
   511→
   512→## Common Parameters Quick Reference
   513→
   514→### DOP Crowd Solver Tabs
   515→
   516→| Tab | Key Parameters |
   517→|-----|---------------|
   518→| Simulation | `substeps`, `maxspeed`, `maxrotspeed`, `maxaccel` |
   519→| Avoidance | `avoidanceforce`, `anticipatetime`, `neighbordist`, `maxneighbors`, `fov` |
   520→| Terrain | `terrain`, `terrainobject`, `enablefootlocking`, `adjusthips` |
   521→| Locomotion | `locomotion`, `locomotionnode`, `gait` |

// Seek toward a target point
vector target   = chv("target_pos");
float max_speed = ch("max_speed");
float seek_wt   = ch("seek_weight");
vector desired  = normalize(target - @P) * max_speed;
vector steer    = desired - @v;
@force += steer * seek_wt;

// Flee from a threat within radius
vector threat     = chv("threat_pos");
float flee_radius = ch("flee_radius");
float flee_force  = ch("flee_force");
float dist        = distance(@P, threat);
if (dist < flee_radius) {
    vector flee_dir = normalize(@P - threat);
    float falloff   = 1.0 - dist / flee_radius;
    @force += flee_dir * flee_force * falloff;
}

// Separation: push agents apart if too close (supplement built-in avoidance)
float sep_radius = ch("sep_radius");
float sep_force  = ch("sep_force");
int neighbors[] = pcfind(0, "P", @P, sep_radius, 8);

    vector diff = @P - point(0, "P", nb);
